title: The Lost Party Basket Adventure
markdown:
The afternoon was the sort that makes a garden forget it has ever been anything but a party. The sky was the brightest blue. Clouds drifted like friendly sheep that had nowhere urgent to be. Mabel the piglet stood by the garden table with her rosy cheeks glowing and her snout doing a happy little snuffle. Beside her, Pompom the poodle looked as if a marshmallow had rolled through a pile of happy thoughts. His tail kept time all by itself. Swish-swish-swish.

“Party time,” Mabel squealed, her curly tail spinning like a spring.

“Yummy treats,” Pompom barked, in his very polite poodle way.

They skipped toward the table, imagining platters piled high. Then they stopped. The big woven picnic basket was not there. Not a sandwich. Not a cupcake with a cherry. Mabel’s snout twitched. Her ears drooped a tiny bit. Pompom tilted his head until his ears flopped like velvet curtains.

“Where did it go?” he whispered.

Mabel spotted something fluttery and bright. A sunny yellow ribbon, just like the one on her favorite party hat. Then another. A splash of sky-blue velvet, soft and smooth, lying further on.

“Look, Pompom.” She pointed with her snout. “Ribbons. And bows. Like sparkly floaty stepping stones.”

They were strung together, a colorful wiggly clue. Pompom’s nose twitched. He could almost smell the adventure.

“Someone left a trail. And it leads that way.” He pointed toward the big shady oak at the far end of the garden, a place usually reserved for quiet naps and important squirrel meetings.

“An adventure,” Mabel declared. Off they trotted, the trot turning into a happy little race. They zoomed past bouncy daisies that tickled their noses. “Achoo!” Mabel sneezed, a tiny puff of pink dust. Pompom, with his delicate paws, had to leap the wibbly-wobbly stepping stones and do a little jig to keep his balance.

“Careful,” Mabel giggled. “Those stones are a bit wobbly-jiggly.”

Pompom’s tail wagged faster, a happy pendulum.

Closer to the oak, the leaves rustled. A tiny sound came from the roots. Chitter-chatter-giggle. Not a scary sound. A sound like happy secrets being whispered by the wind.

“Someone’s there,” Pompom whispered, his tail giving a hopeful wag.

They tiptoed like little shadows on the grass and peeked around the knobbly trunk.

There, nestled in the mossy roots, was the party basket, overflowing like a treasure chest. Sitting right on top, with a shiny red ribbon tied around his neck like a dapper bow tie, was Pip the squirrel. He was trying to balance a tiny cupcake, complete with a sprinkle, on his nose. It wobbled. Splat. The cupcake tumbled and landed with a tiny squish. Pip giggled, his whole body wiggling.

Mabel and Pompom giggled too. Pip looked up, beady eyes wide, twitchy tail frozen mid-wiggle.

“Oh. You found me. This is the bestest toy ever. Look at all the colors. And the smells.” He sniffed a biscuit.

Mabel trotted forward, her snuffle warm. “Hello, Pip. That’s our party basket. It’s almost tea time, and our friends are waiting for the treats inside.”

Pip’s whiskers drooped. “I thought it was a surprise for me. All the pretty things.”

Mabel’s piggy heart felt a tiny ache for him.

“It is a surprise,” said Pompom, stepping forward with a confident wag. He nudged Pip gently. “A surprise for everyone to share. Would you like to come to the party with us? You can help carry the basket. And you can have the first bite of a cupcake.”

Pip’s eyes lit like two little stars. “Really? Yes. Yes, please. I love parties.”

He looked at the wobbly cupcake, then at their hopeful faces. He really wanted to eat it all. Then he carefully handed the slightly squished cupcake to Mabel. A happy feeling bloomed in him, brighter than any ribbon.

They carried the basket back together, Pip scampering beside them, his red ribbon bouncing. The clue-ribbons fluttered behind like decorations cheering them on. They arrived just as the fuzzy bunnies, the sleepy hedgehogs, and one friendly frog were gathering, tummies rumbling.

“Hooray,” everyone cheered when they saw the basket. Mabel, Pompom, and Pip set it down. The cheer grew louder.

Mabel’s snout twitched. She did not make a speech about sharing. She only watched Pip show a hedgehog how to balance a cupcake on a nose before taking a bite. The sandwiches tasted extra yummy. The ribbons from the trail ended up tied to the table legs, flapping whenever anyone laughed. Pip’s red bow stayed on. The afternoon filled itself with snuffles, polite barks, and the particular sound a garden makes when a mix-up has turned into a party after all.
